unmapped_findings: The 6 wt.% Al variant is an intermediate Al content of the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-xAl RAP set and is only very weakly affected by the applied aging treatments in terms of mechanical data, compared with the Al-free Fe-30Mn-1.2C alloy (weakening/embrittlement) and Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al (strengthening) (b0024).

For the 30 wt.% Mn system, high amounts of Al (~8 wt.%) result in pronounced strengthening during aging attributed to nm-sized κ-carbides; the intermediate 2–6 wt.% Al variants do not show equivalent mechanical properties and show a much smaller influence of aging on tensile behavior (b0025).

Figure 5 (APT + TEM κ-carbide analysis after 24 h at 600 °C) is explicitly stated to be for the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al low-density steel, not for the 6 wt.% Al sample; therefore its κ-carbide rod/platelet observations are excluded from this 6Al sample (b0034, figure_005).
Reference (Al-free Fe-30Mn-1.2C) as-homogenized mechanical values reported as context: 360 MPa YS, 830 MPa UTS, 77% TE (b0023).

General density trend from Fig. 1: mass density falls from roughly the 7.15 g/cm³ level near 6 wt.% Al to ~6.4 g/cm³ near 13 wt.% Al; this is a general Fe-Mn-Al-C trend, not a sample-specific measurement for Fe-30Mn-1.2C-6Al (figure_001).
